name: LEAPER (Leveraging Endogenous ADAR for Programmable Editing of RNA)
therapeuticGoalDescription: Correct pathogenic RNA mutations through endogenous ADAR-mediated A→I (G) editing without introducing exogenous editing proteins.
molecularDefect: Single-nucleotide pathogenic variants that can be corrected by adenosine-to-inosine (A→I) RNA editing.
diseaseMechanism: An engineered ADAR-recruiting RNA (arRNA) hybridizes to the target transcript, forming a dsRNA structure that recruits endogenous ADAR enzymes, resulting in site-specific A→I editing.
suitableVariantTypes: G→A pathogenic variants; nonsense mutations; selected missense mutations; splice-site variants correctable by A→I editing.
typicalDiseases: Hurler syndrome (IDUA); Ornithine transcarbamylase (OTC) deficiency; Rett syndrome (MECP2); proof-of-concept studies in additional monogenic disorders.
rnaTargetRegion: Exonic or splice-site regions containing an editable adenosine.
transcriptRequirement: Target transcript must contain an accessible adenosine suitable for endogenous ADAR editing.
typicalLength: Approximately 70–200 nt, depending on target and arRNA design.
designRules: Select an editable adenosine; optimize mismatch opposite the target A; maximize endogenous ADAR recruitment while minimizing bystander editing; validate by RNA sequencing.
secondaryStructureRequirement: Stable duplex formation between arRNA and target RNA is required for efficient ADAR recruitment.
offTargetConsiderations: Bystander A→I editing; transcriptome-wide off-target editing; RNA duplex-dependent specificity.
advantages: No exogenous protein delivery; reversible RNA editing; reduced risk of permanent genomic alterations.
limitations: Restricted to editable adenosines; editing efficiency varies by transcript and cell type; no approved therapies.
